title: A three-manifold without conjugate points
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: An exposition of OpenAI's proof (2026) that there is a closed connected orientable smooth three-manifold that carries a Riemannian metric without conjugate points but no metric of nonpositive sectional curvature. The manifold consists of two copies of a holed torus times a circle, glued through a collar so that h_2 = h_1 + f_1 and f_2 = h_1. The first lesson fixes conventions, proves the index-form criterion for the absence of conjugate points and the assembly of estimates over the visits of a geodesic to a region, and states the theorem. The second builds the manifold, checks orientability, and computes its fundamental group with van Kampen's theorem and normal forms in amalgamated products. The third develops the geometry of complete geodesic spaces with the CN inequality of Bruhat and Tits (CAT(0) spaces and Hadamard manifolds): uniqueness and convexity of geodesics, the four-point inequality, projections, an exact Pythagorean identity for parallel lines and additive shifts. The fourth proves that isometries commuting with a hyperbolic isometry have a shift homomorphism and, for shift zero, a Pythagorean length formula; the two pieces then give incompatible formulas, so the fundamental group has no proper cocompact action on a proper CAT(0) space and the manifold has no nonpositively curved metric. The fifth constructs the metric: a concave cometric on the neck, warped convex collars and flat cores. The sixth and seventh prove that the index form is nonnegative on every visit of a geodesic to the neck: tangential gauges and the endpoint correction for crossings, and for returning geodesics a Hilbert-space duality with a timing margin that is uniform in all parameters.
prerequisites: course DG-FND, lesson Jacobi fields, conjugate points and the Morse index theorem: the Jacobi equation (Theorem A.1), the second variation of energy (Theorem A.4), nonpositive curvature has no conjugate points (Corollary F.3), the Morse index theorem (Theorem D.1, exercises only)

open_obligations: Named hypothesis (MCH): the metric Cartan-Hadamard theorem with the Hopf-Rinow theorem for length spaces (proofs in Poulsen, arXiv:2406.09883, Theorems 3.5.1 and 1.3.5). Used only for Corollary 4.3 of the fourth lesson (no locally CAT(0) length metric); not proved in the programme.

Ivanov-Kapovitch, arXiv:1205.4455, Theorem 7.1 (a closed three-manifold carries a metric without focal points exactly when it carries one of nonpositive curvature): used only for the remark on focal points; not proved in the programme.

Missing foundation: a course on CAT(0) spaces with the flat strip and flat torus theorems and the metric Cartan-Hadamard theorem would close (MCH) and give the flat geometry behind the length formula; the main theorem does not need it.
The lessons were written and checked by one model in one session; they have not been checked by a second reader.
